He noticed my disturbance and believed it was because of what he was saying to me; in a severe tone he said to me: «Produce the documents, and they will be verified.»

Confused, I answered yes, but within myself (I thought): what can this man want to do with the documents? I no longer remembered what I had said. But the scene was not yet over; two other strangers came in and, worse than the first, they had sackfuls of things to say to me. One may well consider that if they had beaten me with sticks, I would have felt little or nothing. At last, tired of talking and having put together all their inventions, they dismissed me, telling me to return with the documents.

My God! Along the way, pressed close to my Beloved, I no longer remembered anything; one by one I repeated his words to myself and, as if he were still with me, I pondered them, but quite other than what I had received.

In aid of the plants that, eaten away by the worm, cannot bear good fruit.

Oh! without noticing it I found myself at my cottage; I would still have liked to tell him so many things, but all of a sudden he took his union away from me, and I remained utterly a poor creature surrounded by an immense labor, and all of it material.

Where am I? There, plants that are falling; over there, vines full of shoots without grapes, great flowering plants without a single flower, other trees full of dry branches…; a scourge of people, every one of whose actions was a greater damage.

Who ever reduced this poor field to so bad a state? My Lord, is this not yours too? how did these evildoers allow themselves to reduce it in this way? The plants are yours!

Looking to one side, I see two that are falling down. Without heeding anything else, I run and, with the strength of my God, I raise them and replant them; holding them firmly, I take a strong support and tie them tightly. While I am doing this work, I see them blossoming gracefully and promising very well.

I go near to prune those trees that have so many dry branches; I cut away a large portion of them; at the end there remained certain little stumps near the ground: I bend down to remove them — oh! out comes a serpent, not very large. How angry it was! It tries everything to bite me, but does not succeed. It coils round the tree and does not move, out of hunger. I try to kill it: no! It made horrid noises, and meanwhile other branches were drying up. Oh! how sorry I felt! It was a fine tree, and seeing it so reduced grieved me more than ever. I was cutting off the trunks, when I took the pincers and seized that snake that wanted to bite me, and cut it to pieces. The tree began to grow again and to put out fine branches.

I passed on to another, but I could not manage to remove the dry branches: I took away one, and others dried up. I looked at the roots and found nothing there; but I saw that it must have something that kept it well hidden. I gave the tree a heavy blow with a large club: oh! under the bark there were certain little worms, like very tiny serpents, with two sharp horns and so fierce that they tried to bite me; and the more I drove them away, the more they multiplied in an extraordinary way. Meanwhile the tree was drying up: how was I to free it? I called upon the Most High with strong supplications, but these creatures seemed to me to grow more venomous. At last: «In the name of God, withdraw! go back where you came from, and leave this plant free!»

They scattered and left the plant free. The poor thing raised itself up again.

I went to another, which besides having dry branches was ugly, and almost made me shudder to touch it. Moved by compassion, I went near it and, looking at it very carefully, (I said to myself): how must I begin to clean it? My God! it is damaged on every side. I cut off branches, and just as many died. I saw that there was something there. I began to pray, asking God to make known to me where the evil lay. A voice said to me: «In the pith!»

«How must I go about removing it? must I cut the tree down to the roots?»

«No!»

«Must I abandon it?»

«No! It too was created by me, and tended. Try everything to reach the pith, and you will save it.»

So I did. But the obstinacy of the worms that had worked their way in was such that I could not get to the end of it. Resolute, I turned to it: «Either give up that sap, or I will cut you down!

The shock, the fear, caused an abundance of sap to come out.

Tired, I would have liked to take some rest, but for fear that those that still remained might dry up altogether, I went on. While I was approaching another plant to heal it, I see that there was a woman there who wanted to adorn it according to her own taste. But I cried out: «Away! this tree belongs to my Master and you have nothing more to do with it. Go away, if you do not wish both of you to be lost.»

But whatever I did, I achieved nothing. I began to be dismayed, thinking of that beautiful plant. I saw that the woman had an evil spirit, which was whispering to her to uproot the tree and carry it away. Oh! I began to cry out: «What are you doing? Never let it be! this plant no longer belongs to you; you have made a gift of it to the Lord, and it cannot be uprooted except with great harm to it and to you, for you will see it dry up on the way. No!»

But it was not the poor woman herself (who was acting), but rather that evil spirit that was whispering to her, saying: «Carry it away!»

The plant, moreover, bent very willingly to be carried away; it did not dare to resist. Meanwhile that dragon insisted with all its power; in the end it won, because there was much consent on the part of the plant itself. What sorrow! the plant is uprooted and carried away; but on the way it dries up; although replanted, it no longer gives any fruit. Useless tree!

The woman (remained) grieved, because that dragon, having gained its end, withdrew, sure of its success, namely that the plant will no longer bear fruit for Jesus, but will always remain in danger of withering eternally. Oh! how pitiable was the state of the woman and of the tree! there are no phrases to describe their anguish. The woman could not be at peace, that she should so soon have had the disillusionment and the remorse of having taken from the garden of the Lord a plant which, if set right again, could certainly have given exquisite fruit.

Patience! How great is the goodness my God has for souls! And we, ungrateful creatures? Oh! how can I ever manage to make myself understood, so that all may cease to offend you and may love you!

Very sorrowful, I went to other plants, and yet I put all my attention into working them well and removing from around them the weeds that were eating away the roots. I saw one that had fared worse than the others; it seemed to be dying of thirst: the leaves withered, the branches drooping… It moved me to compassion. I took hold of it to see about straightening it, but I could not understand on which side its trouble lay; I went round and round it, but never came to the decision to set my hand to it; I watered it, but nothing! It was inert; it gave no sign of wanting to regain its vigor: nothing! What was I to do? I tried removing the leaves: nothing! I looked at it on every side to see if it had a worm, but I could not find where it was. Finally, I water it heavily. It seemed to me to revive, but this was for a short time. I grieved greatly over it. At last my voice: «Look into its pith, and you will see that it holds a very tiny worm, and it is the plant itself that keeps it with pleasure, because it feels satisfaction in being thus infirm.

I did not delay to take the worm from it, and at once it recovered, but very unwillingly. And it cost much to make it less inert; it bore fruit, but very scarce and many of them wretched, and so many fell to the ground, because it would not give them enough sap to make them beautiful; and this sap is most precious and brings the fruits very well to ripeness. Oh! how easily this grace is allowed to be lost! The plants of our garden, according to the labor of the precious Gardener, ought all to be flourishing and to give tasty fruits to the Master. Oh! how different it is! One languishes, one withers, and a great number remain small, without growth. How (full) of shame they will be when they find themselves before their Master with those fruits ranged before them, which will accuse them of every one of their failings! Horrible blindness!

I had not yet finished setting these trees right when, tired, I fell asleep at the foot of one that was large but without fruit. I said to myself: The season will not yet have come. Overcome by sleep, I fell asleep and, dreaming, I was given the story of the tree: why it had not borne fruit. When I awoke, I called a good worker: we transplanted it, and with patience and much charity, well watered, it was not long in putting forth its flowers. With the hope of having a fine harvest, (I went away), recommending to the overseer to take care that it should not lack nourishment and that from time to time she should seek a good shepherd who would know how to cultivate it according to the will of God.

On the one hand, she feels limited, in need of a guide, precisely because her road is exceptional; and there is no lack of learned men, considered saints, who would like to come to her aid; but she at once realizes that their roads, although often parallel, are different from hers.
